hints.S60_A1: Her determination is measured against STEEL, and NOTHING COULD SHAKE HER BELIEF. Ask: which word describes something that cannot be bent or broken? 'Weak' is its opposite, and 'heavy' and 'cold' describe metal, not willpower.
hints.S60_A2: If you MUST BE READY TO GRAB THEM WITH BOTH HANDS the moment they appear, such chances must be rare. Ask: which idiom means 'hardly ever'? 'Every day' says the exact opposite, and 'on purpose' means done deliberately.
hints.S60_A3: The class feels GREAT EXCITEMENT about a ceremony that is still ahead of them, AT THE END OF EACH YEAR. Ask: which phrasal verb means to await something happily? 'Forget', 'give up on' and 'run away from' all turn away from it.
hints.S60_A4: She TURNED EVERY FAILURE INTO A NEW IDEA and NEVER STOPPED TRYING. Ask: which word names the quality of keeping on despite setbacks? 'Speed', 'silence' and 'caution' say nothing about refusing to quit.
hints.S60_A5: A scientist does not simply hand out LIFE-SAVING MEDICINES - she must bring them into existence through research. Ask: which verb means to create something new? 'Copy' repeats what exists, and 'remove' takes something away.
hints.S60_B1: The subject is NO ONE, however many classmates sit around. Ask: in the present tense, does a singular subject take the plain verb, or the one ending in -s? 'No one' behaves like a single person, exactly as 'everyone' does.
hints.S60_B2: 'HAS' is printed before the blank, so the pair must build a present perfect. Ask: after 'has', do we use the plain verb, the -s form, the -ing form, or the past participle? This verb is regular, so its ending is predictable.
hints.S60_B3: Read the words already there: THE MOST. The superlative is built for you, so the blank needs the plain adjective. Ask: may you ever stack 'more' or an -er ending on top of 'the most'? One comparison marker is enough.
hints.S60_B4: THE PRINCIPAL WALKED INTO THE HALL - a sudden arrival that cut across the practice. Ask: which choice shows an action still in progress in the PAST? The speeches were not finished when the door opened.
hints.S60_B5: ROOM FOR DOUBT cannot be counted - there is no such thing as 'two rooms for doubt' - and Priya KNOWS EXACTLY what she wants. Ask: which choice goes with an uncountable noun to mean 'hardly any'? 'Few' and 'many' need countable things.
hints.S60_B6: The statement is positive and its verb TAKES is a plain present verb - there is no 'is' or 'has' to echo. Ask: which helping verb stands in for a plain present verb, and does a positive statement take a positive tag or a negative one?
hints.S60_B7: THE AWARD cannot hand itself over - the school did that, LAST YEAR. Ask: which choice is passive (the subject receives the action) and set in the past? There is only one award, so the helping verb must be singular.
hints.S60_B8: ASKED THE STUDENTS = a reported request, and it is about THE SUBJECTS THAT INTERESTED THEM MOST. Ask: after 'asked + person', which form follows - the plain verb, the -ing form, or 'to' + verb? Pick the full infinitive.
hints.S60_C1: The subject is EVERY CHILD - one child at a time, even though there are millions of them. Ask: in the simple present, does a singular subject take the plain verb or the one wearing -s? Every box entry is the same verb; only the ENDING differs.
hints.S60_C2: Look at the words before the blank: SPENT ALL OF SATURDAY. Ask: after 'spend + a length of time', which form of the verb follows - the plain one, the one with 'to' in front, or the one ending in -ing?
hints.S60_C3: LAST NIGHT is finished time, and nothing cuts across the event - it is over and done with. Ask: which box entry is a simple past form standing alone, with no helping verb beside it? A past continuous always needs a partner.
hints.S60_C4: WHILE opens a long background action, and HER TEACHER NOTICED cuts across it. Ask: which box entry shows one girl in the middle of something in the past? Watch the helping verb - the subject is only SHE.
hints.S60_C5: ALL THE CHILDREN is plural, and THE BELL RANG interrupted them in the middle of something. Ask: which box entry shows a past action still in progress AND carries a plural helping verb? Count the subject before you choose.
hints.S60_C6: Look at the pattern: IT IS NEVER TOO EARLY ___ BIG. Ask: after 'too early', 'too late' or 'too tired', which form always follows - the one ending in -ing, or the infinitive with its little word in front? Say it aloud.
hints.S60_C7: The words TOLD HER TO are already printed in front of the blank. Ask: after the little word 'to', which form of a verb may ever follow - the plain one, the one with -s, or the one with -ing? An infinitive takes no ending.
hints.S60_C8: FOR YEARS TO COME points ahead, not backwards - none of this has happened yet. Ask: which box entry is set in the FUTURE? A present or past form cannot reach into years that have not arrived.
hints.S60_D1: The dash defines it: A DEEP DESIRE TO ACHIEVE SOMETHING GREAT that KEEPS A PERSON GOING THROUGH HARD TIMES. The blank follows 'a strong', so it must be a noun. Ask: which box word names that inner drive?
hints.S60_D2: The dash explains it: SOMEONE YOU LOOK UP TO. Ask: which box entry names a person you admire and want to copy? The other entries name a feeling, a drive or an action - not a human being.
hints.S60_D3: SUCH A PERSON makes you TRY HARDER AND REACH HIGHER. The blank follows 'can', so it must be a plain verb. Ask: which box word means to fill someone with the will to do great things?
hints.S60_D4: They IMPROVE THEMSELVES EVERY DAY, SETTING SMALL GOALS. The subject is plural, so the blank must be a plain verb. Ask: which box word means to make a great and steady effort towards a goal?
hints.S60_D5: The dash tells you plainly: THE ACTIVITY THAT EXCITES YOU MOST. It follows 'your true', so it must be a noun. Ask: which box word names the thing you love doing above everything else?
hints.S60_E1: Look at who was excited: THE STUDENTS, from the moment she walked in. Ask: is the underlined verb singular or plural, and which one does a plural subject need? Agreement is settled by the subject, nothing else.
hints.S60_E2: The sentence is about enduring THE PRESSURE OF TRAINING, not about being uncovered or empty. Ask: which spelling means 'to carry or put up with something'? The same word also names a large furry animal.
hints.S60_E3: 'BREIF' has its vowels in the wrong order. Ask: which comes first in this word, the I or the E? Remember: I before E, except after C - the same order as in chief, niece and grief.
hints.S60_E4: The underlined word describes HOW the astronaut SPOKE, and it is paired with 'and CLEARLY', which already wears the right ending. Ask: after an action verb, do we need an adjective or an adverb? Make the pair match.
hints.S60_E5: 'CHILDRENS' is not a word: CHILDREN is already plural without any -s. Ask: when a plural does not end in -s, where does the apostrophe go, and what follows it? Compare: the men's team, the women's race.
hints.S60_F1: 'AFTER' must sit in front of the EARLIER event. Ask: which came first - the daily practice, or becoming the most confident presenter? Both halves share one subject, so the verb after 'after' may take an -ing ending.
hints.S60_F2: Sentence B is a question aimed at Kai: 'WHAT DO YOU WANT TO BE WHEN YOU GROW UP?' Ask: once it is reported, who does 'you' become, and does the helper 'do' survive? The word 'asked' also pulls the verbs back into the past.
